left.title: Transport Secretary Elaine Chao Still Owns Road-Paving Company Stock She Promised To Get Rid Of
left.body: Transport Secretary Elaine Chao could be in for a bumpy ride after The Wall Street Journal reported that she still owns stock in a road-paving company, more than a year after she promised to get rid of it. Chao’s holdings are in Vulcan Materials, which is the largest U.S. supplier of stone, sand, and gravel used in road-paving and building. The stock price has risen nearly 13 percent since April 2018, the month Chao said she would ditch the shares, meaning she’s gained more $40,000 since the promise was made .
left.roundup: Secretary of Transportation Elaine Chao has not divested her stocks in a construction company, as she had promised to do. Chao has not sold her stocks and dissolved her ties with Vulcan Materials, she is still reported to have about $400,000 of stock in the company. She has been estimated to have made about $40,000 since making a promise to divest. It is unknown whether the ethics agreement that she signed implies that she must 'disentangle' herself from the asphalt company, in order to avoid any conflict of interest. It is well noted that Sec. Chao is married to Senate Majority Leader Mitch McConnell (R-KY).

center.title: Report: Elaine Chao still owns shares in stock she promised to divest
center.body: Transportation Secretary Elaine Chao reportedly still owns stock in a construction company that she previously promised to divest from upon taking office. The Wall Street Journal reported Tuesday that federal disclosure forms show Chao to be the owner of nearly $400,000 worth of stock in Vulcan Materials Co., a major supplier of materials for road pavement and other construction projects, more than a year after she promised to trade the shares for a cash payout. right.title: Transportation Sec. Elaine Chao Under Fire For Reportedly Failing To Cut Ties With Construction Materials Company
right.body: Transportation Secretary Elaine Chao is under fire for reportedly retaining shares in a construction materials company following a Tuesday story in The Wall Street Journal headlined she had “pledged to divest.” Chao agreed to take a “cash payout” in April 2018 for her shares in road materials giant Vulcan Materials Co. per a January 2017 ethics agreement prior to her confirmation.
